mappings.rationale: Supplier name is a business name from a procurement disclosure. The source does not confirm it is the as-registered name, so this is a weak semantic mapping. Held-out values show trailing-punctuation and trust-style forms (e.g. 'A MARINOV & J.D MARINOV T/A'), which are not clean registered legal names. Confidence lowered below the minimum; the field is left for human decision.

Header explicitly names the supplier ABN and the abn transform enforces checksum. Held-out values include spaced forms ('49 096 776 895'), which the abn transform normalises. Coverage is sparse (4 of 300 held-out rows), which does not reduce mapping confidence; absent values emit nothing.

Values are 4-digit Australian postcodes. The 49 held-out errors all have a leading zero-width space (U+200B, mis-decoded as 'â€‹') before the postcode, plus one value 'Vari' that is not a postcode. Stripping the invisible prefix and enforcing the postcode transform is the fix; the 'Vari' row is a non-postcode value and will remain rejected.

warnings: Supplier name mapping to entity.legal_name is unverified; confidence set to 0.7, below the 0.8 minimum, so it should be excluded from emission until a register check or human sign-off.

Supplier address postcode errors in held-out data are caused by a leading U+200B zero-width space (mis-decoded). Strip handles this only if the transform removes it; if the engine's strip does not remove zero-width characters, these 48 rows will keep failing and this must be verified.
One held-out value 'Vari' in Supplier address appears to be a mis-aligned value from the Variation column; the row is likely shifted or malformed and should be reviewed at source.
No observed_at field in source; observed_at is the resource last-modified proxy and must not be used as a statement time.
No ACN source column; ACN must not be inferred from ABN.
